component: P04-13 Bridge save/baseline/cancellation and public read/save DTO integration
reviewer: error_codec; integration author root. Reviewer-authored new core codec is context only, separately independently reviewed by error_oracle.

reviewed_properties.evidence: Bridge save requires nonnull packet/preferences, nonzero matching GUI-published Host session and nonzero request; validates exact bounded native preferences before making an owned const copy for the worker. Worker independently checks the same actual Host session and held baseline. Window capture/save uses a separate monotonic request counter, captures pane revisions and retains one active save; read/save queues mutually guard active commands. Ordinary library revision does not authorize or retarget a save.

Host alone owns pristine baseline/source on its existing worker. Optional layout read clears prior baseline before IO, stores only the successful owned raw source and actual source enum. Missing/failed reads never fabricate a baseline. Save adapter requires Primary baseline and fresh Primary load, exact complete raw byte equality and pristine source consistency; recovery/Missing/external byte changes fail before writing. Success returns preallocated pristine baseline, used for later exact-byte saves. Save error clears Host baseline/source, requiring explicit reload.

Only native preference key is passed to the pure writer; no canonical original column key, file geometry, torrent value, model revision or transfer action is written. Root original table/plugin raw preservation is delegated to the newly independently reviewed pure codec plus qualified Document/ConfigFile boundaries. Only fixed tables.config uses held lease; no new profile discovery/lease/path chase/network/thread.

Stop checked before worker operation and by adapter through preparation/pre-save; prepared success Document parse/shared ownership is allocated before ConfigFile::save. Once synchronous save begins, no adapter/Bridge post-save cancellation checkpoint converts a real commit into Cancelled. Bridge save callback always publishes actual saved/failure packet, including after stop. If Executor skips an accepted cancelled command, existing no-posted monitor releases busy without inventing a successful save; Window clears active save and asks reload.

Save packet emitted while busy remains true, rejecting direct command reentry; QPointer tested immediately after signal before monitor/busy access. Busyfalse is last emission in the save callback. Optional read similarly rechecks queued stop/session, guards callback deletion and remains busy through packet delivery. No GUI widget or borrowed capture crosses to worker; QObject-bound queued delivery cannot run after receiver destruction. Destruction cancels/joins worker before Host/lease fields by existing member order.

reviewed_properties.area: Read/private preference precedence and defensive DTOs
reviewed_properties.evidence: Ready Window packets require valid source enum, nonnull snapshot/raw source and validateClassicPreferences when private data is present. Native preferences select full private layout; absent preferences retain source-derived whitelist import. Matching session/request required before consuming active request; stale packets cannot consume current one. Per-pane edit revisions/current-request guard retain later local edits and stop direct callback reentry/deletion. UI never reparses source data or invents original Java equivalence.

Matching save packet clears only its active save. Successful acknowledgement compares captured/current pane revisions to distinguish saved current layout from earlier saved layout with newer unsaved edits. It does not apply saved headers or retarget selection/details. Failed/no-packet outcomes disable saving until reload; successful actual result permits the new worker baseline. Rejected/unconnected request is released without latching. Close/deferred-close and independent service/read queues retain existing busy/cancellation behavior.

qualification_limits: Full source/hash review only. Reviewer performed no compiler/preprocessor, selected target evaluation, GUI/native/test/process/JVM/profile/network or file-save execution. No actual result credited here.

Existing owner-thread API precondition applies; no cross-thread concurrent GUI facade mutation claim. Memory/Qt delivery failure does not prove publication under allocation failure; a missing result remains an explicit reload-required failure, not an unchanged-file promise.

ConfigFile remains a cooperative held-directory byte-conflict check with existing recovery/error stages, not primary-inode CAS, multi-file transaction or stronger durability. Errors after rename can imply replacement occurred.

Private native preferences do not claim original registered-column/layout/comparator application, Java manager runtime retention, whole-root reset survival or canonical-column writing. Original Java normal-save semantic roundtrip remains a separate source/runtime gate.
Root owns actual unit/Qt/sanitizer/generated-profile/end-to-end qualification and publication; this PASS does not assert those executions.
